## Summary

The specification required all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) to return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

The 409 (`CityAtCapacity`, `DuplicateIdentity`) and 429 (`DailyOwnerLimit`) handlers already emitted `ProblemDetail` bodies via the existing `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper, as did the schema-validation 400 handler. But six field-level 400 handlers still returned a bespoke `FieldErrorsResponse` (`{"errors":[...]}`) plain-JSON body:

- `MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler`
- `DisposableEmailDomainExceptionHandler`
- `FutureRegistrationDateExceptionHandler`
- `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler`
- `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler`
- `InvalidTelephoneExceptionHandler`

I converted each to reuse the existing `ProblemDetails.build(ex, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, ex.getMessage())` helper and send a `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` — the same pattern the 409/429 handlers already follow, so Spring emits `application/problem+json` with the four required members. Using each exception's own message as `detail` keeps a single source of truth (and `MissingOwnerFieldsException`'s message still names the offending fields, so no information is lost). The HTTP status codes are unchanged.

With no remaining references, I deleted the now-unused `FieldErrorsResponse` record so the escalation package doesn't carry a dead second error-body shape.

The new acceptance test `coreRejectionIsProblemJson` (missing `city` → 400) and all existing tests pass.
